text: Does backlogit currently handle the update of all YAML header values in target markdown files through existing MCP tooling? And is that tooling well described so that the agent can determine when to effectively use it to offload effort?
The stash fetch-stash command needs to be changed to stash list: much easier to type, non-redundant, simple verb action.  Should also include a --filter command for priority and kind.

For backlogit, we also want to make sure that we include in the log of events the commit ID associated with changes. For example, the JSON log of events should be prefixed with the ID of the task being referenced, should include the time stamp on the file name, and include a commit ID and an explanation of the work done that allows a tool to process these programmatically and synchronize them with end-user systems such as Azure DevOps or Jira or GitHub issues.

The stash command also needs a get item, as in get a specific item by its stash ID. It needs to have an edit command that takes as a parameter the stash ID and the new text to use, as well as edits to the kind. There needs to be a stash list command that does not already exist, and this should be true at the CLI as well as the MCP tool set. Also, I think we need to fix the priority argument for this -add command, because it doesn't seem to work; it breaks, so we need to fix that. We need to be able to add that to be stashed so we can change the priority and kind when we edit a stash item.

The backlog tool needs another kind of enum type for the stash command. If I write backlogit stash add and some text, then I need to have also kind 'unknown'. This should allow the agent to help determine whether this stash item is actually at a feature level, at a task level, or something else. Maybe it's a bug.

For the backlogit tool, we want the agent to review the way we store work items in the queue. Should we prefix each item, for example, with a T or F  or ST, etc., or should we structure the items only at the beginning of the file names with their number level, such as 001.001.001, and then a dash and then the artifact type, such as review or feature or task or subtask? There are potentially advantages to only having the first part of the name be in a strict syntactical order so that all work items are easily sorted at the file system level. They all show and group together naturally in a view. Some additional considerations: I'm beginning to think it actually makes the most sense to just have the ID of the work item also be the file name of the work item. The related event.jsonl file for that work item also shares the same root file name, just having a separate extension of.jsonl rather than.empty, and then using the enum prefix for each work item type as a suffix at the end of the file name as well as at the end of the ID so that they match.Here's an example. If the work item is a feature and it is a top-level item, it would be 001-FA. A task might be of the same feature, might be 001.001-T. The second task after that same feature might be 001.002-T. A subtask could be 001.001.001-S. A bug on a specific feature could be as simple as 001.001.001-B. Reviews are probably a little different, because they would most likely be at the same level as the feature. For example, that could be 001.001-R. The review might be itself at level two but parented to a feature by design, so that would be 001.001.001-R. The hierarchy is where you determine the lineage of parents and children. If you want to have a review at the task level, or if a review is of a task, it would have to be leveled at a third level, so it would be 001.001.001-R, so that review lineage is two parent tasks as opposed to the parent feature. Actually, that isn't, by convention, really any different from the other work item types, I guess.

The .backlogit directory should be read-only to the agent; only the backlogit CLI or MCP tool should ever write to the directory to ensure correct hygiene in the backlogit work item management.  This will mean adding constraints in the constitution, skills, and agents of the agent harness to ensure correct workflow is maintained.  There should never be generative output directly added to this directory.

For the agent to be able to effectively construct custom sql queries against backlogit.db, it needs a map of the available tables and fields with example queries it can construct for a range of result sets.  These should be added as a custom backlogit.instructions.md file available to the agent.
We should probably add some kind of queue work item archival policy for auto archival of completed work items.  Propose options for this and why each option would make sense.

I think we need a step between stashing an idea to a step where the agent and user develop the idea from the stash item.  In this process, I think the stash entry is developed through the delibration skill and move over to a .queue.md file in the queue folder to register it effectively as a backlog item that is actually ready to be harvested.

I think we need to reconsider the current agent setup.  Right now, the setup is one of multiple agents, but it might make more sense to just have one orchestrating agent that leverages many skills along a specific workflow that starts with entries in the stash as the source input for what gets deliberated on and ultimately pulled into a feature set that goes through the build orchestrator and so on.  In this case, the build orchestrator is no longer its own agent but instead a skill.  Need some adversarial research and thinking on this one.
Two-agent workflow refactor
Derive parent hierarchy from typed IDs where possible, and add structured related_id metadata for non-hierarchical relationships such as deliberation 001-DL linking to feature 015-F.

Generalize hierarchical parenting support for other parented work-item types such as bugs, including correct ID and filename generation, explicit parent validation rules, and regression coverage for non-task child types.

Consider adding richer artifact relationship links across stash entries and backlog items, including related_to and duplicate_of in addition to parent-child. Support linking bugs, features, tasks, and other items to each other, and expose link management through CLI and MCP commands.
Orphaned work item identity: status-as-authority with parent_id nulled on feature release return

Harden stash harvest against race conditions: add advisory file locking or DB-level dedup guard (INSERT WHERE NOT EXISTS stash_links) to prevent duplicate artifact creation when two sessions harvest the same stash entry concurrently. Current TOCTOU window exists between .stash.md parse and atomic rewrite in internal/core/stash.go. Consider harvest journal pattern for crash recovery similar to return-blocked journals.

Orphan detection tool: add a dedicated MCP tool or SQL view that identifies queued/active items whose parent_id references an archived, done, or nonexistent feature. This is a core grooming operation that currently requires manual SQL joins.

Duplicate artifact detection: add a query or tool that finds items with identical titles but different IDs, especially across legacy and current ID formats. The ID migration left behind duplicates that pollute the queue and confuse triage.

Rehydration creates ghost index entries from JSONL log files even when no corresponding markdown artifact exists. F016.T008-T014 appear in the index but have no markdown source files -- only .jsonl logs. This violates the CQRS principle that markdown is the source of truth. Rehydration should only index items with durable markdown files.

Need a way to implement disaster recovery of agent session ending suddenly, which can happen when using a remote server or if the power gets shut off.  This may involve a combination of agent harness improvements and backlogit tooling.  Need to perform adequate research and analysis to understand what this feature entails.
